verses.text: There was a prominent man from Benjamin named Kish. He was the son of Abiel, son of Zeror, son of Becorath, son of Aphiah, a Benjaminite.
Kish had a son named Saul, an impressive young man. Nobody in Israel was more handsome than Saul, and he stood a head taller than everyone else.
One day Kish's donkeys went missing. He told Saul, “Take one of the servants with you and go look for the donkeys.”
They traveled through Ephraim's hill country and the land of Shalishah without finding them. They went through Shaalim and then through Benjamin's territory, but the donkeys were nowhere to be found.
When they reached the land of Zuph, Saul told his servant, “Let's go home before my father stops worrying about the donkeys and starts worrying about us.”
The servant said, “There's a man of God in this town. People respect him, and everything he says comes true. Let's go see him. Maybe he can tell us where to go.”
Saul asked, “If we go, what can we bring him? The bread in our bags is gone, and we haven't got a gift for the man of God. What do we have?”
The servant said, “I have a quarter shekel of silver. I'll give it to the man of God to show us where to go.”
In earlier days in Israel, when someone wanted to ask God for guidance, they'd say, “Let's go see the seer.” A prophet used to be called a seer.
Saul told his servant, “Good idea. Let's go.” So they headed to the town where the man of God was.
As they went uphill toward the town, they met some young women coming out to draw water and asked, “Is the seer here?”
They answered, “Yes, he's just ahead of you. Hurry. He came to town today because the people are offering a sacrifice at the high place.
When you get into town, you'll find him before he goes up to the high place to eat. The guests wait for him to bless the sacrifice before they eat. Go up now, and you'll find him.”
They went up to the town, and just as they entered, Samuel came out toward them on his way to the high place.
The day before Saul arrived, the LORD had told Samuel,
“Tomorrow about this time I'll send you a man from Benjamin. Anoint him as ruler over my people Israel. He'll rescue them from the Philistines. I've seen my people, and their cries have reached me.”
When Samuel saw Saul, the LORD said to him, “That's the man I told you about. He'll rule over my people.”
Saul approached Samuel at the gate and asked, “Can you tell me where the seer lives?”
Samuel said, “I'm the seer. Go ahead of me to the high place, because you'll eat with me today. In the morning I'll send you on your way and tell you everything that's on your mind.
Don't worry about the donkeys you lost three days ago. They've been found. And who is all Israel looking to? Isn't it you and your father's whole family?”
Saul answered, “I'm from Benjamin, the smallest tribe in Israel, and my family is the least important in Benjamin. Why are you talking to me like this?”
Samuel took Saul and his servant into the guest room and gave them the places of honor among about thirty guests.
Samuel told the cook, “Bring the serving I gave you and asked you to set aside.”

The cook brought out the thigh and what was on it and put it before Saul. Samuel said, “Here is the portion I had set aside. Eat it. It was kept for you for this occasion, when I invited these guests.” So Saul ate with Samuel that day.
After they came down from the high place into town, Samuel spoke with Saul on the roof.
They got up early. Around daybreak Samuel called to Saul on the roof, “Get up, and I'll send you on your way.” Saul got up, and the two went outside together.
As they reached the edge of town, Samuel told Saul to send the servant on ahead. After the servant went on, Samuel said, “Stay here a moment so I can tell you God's message.”
